findings.property: The base-point order is prime, so Pohlig-Hellman has nothing to split
findings.verdict: Pohlig-Hellman costs a full sqrt(n); the largest prime factor is n itself, which the measured smooth-order control confirms from both sides

findings.property: The curve has cofactor 1, so there is no small subgroup to land in
findings.verdict: small-subgroup confinement needs a cofactor > 1; there is none, so the attack has no target

findings.property: #E != p, so the Smart-Satoh-Semenov additive transfer does not apply
findings.verdict: trace != 1, so the curve is not anomalous

findings.property: No small k with p^k = 1 mod n, so MOV/Frey-Ruck has no target field
findings.measured: no k <= 1000 with p^k = 1 (mod n): True
findings.verdict: moving the problem to a finite field needs a small embedding degree; none exists below the probe limit, and the true degree divides n-1

findings.property: The curve is ordinary, so the curve has no low-degree isogeny to a supersingular neighbour
findings.verdict: supersingular curves have trace 0 and small embedding degree; this one has neither

findings.property: The field is prime, so there is no proper subfield to descend to
findings.measured: p = 2^256 - 2^32 - 977, prime; F_p has no proper subfield
findings.verdict: Weil descent needs F_{p^m} with m > 1; prime fields have no such structure

findings.property: The curve is non-singular, so no isomorphism to an additive or multiplicative group exists
findings.verdict: a singular curve would hand the discrete logarithm to F_p^* or F_p^+; the discriminant is 108 != 0

findings.property: The only known exploitable structure is the CM endomorphism of discriminant -3
findings.measured: phi(P) = (beta*x, y) with phi(P) = lambda*P, verified by glv-check
findings.verdict: GLV saves a factor of 2 in the constant of a scalar multiplication and of a rho attack; the exponent stays 1/2, which the measurement confirms

findings.property: No index-calculus algorithm is known for prime-order elliptic curves
findings.measured: best published ECDLP records are generic-group records, not index-calculus records
findings.verdict: summation-polynomial index calculus needs small-degree extension fields; it degrades to worse than rho on a prime field

findings.property: Every algorithm that only uses the group operations needs Omega(sqrt(n))
findings.measured: Nechaev-Shoup lower bound for generic algorithms
findings.verdict: the lower bound is a theorem, so a refutation must use non-generic structure, and the rows above enumerate every known candidate

conclusion: no audited property yields an attack on secp256k1
